deciding_assertions: expect-timeout.spec.ts 'should fail like a timeout when the signal is aborted mid-assertion' and 'should fail the assertion when the signal is already aborted': expect(...).toBeVisible/toHaveURL({signal}) must fail with error.name not 'AbortError' and the exact text 'Error: The assertion was aborted: stop it' / '... already aborted' in the matcher message; page-filechooser.spec.ts 'should abort with signal': waitForEvent rejection must have name 'AbortError' and cause equal to the raw abort reason.
reason: The issue asks for a signal option on waitFor* APIs and gives no error shape. The tests instead check signal on expect() assertions (not waitFor* APIs) with a new exact message 'The assertion was aborted: <reason>', and change waitForEvent's abort error to an AbortError with cause; the packet shows the base waiter already accepted signal and rejected on abort (old test passed with the reason as message). A narrowest reasonable fix that adds signal to waitFor* APIs and rejects with the abort reason fails all three fail-to-pass tests.

deciding_assertions: test-locks.spec.ts: every test declares test('x', { lock: 'shared' | [...] }, body) and test.describe('s', { lock: 'shared' }, ...); 'should validate lock in test details' expects output to contain 'details.lock'; 'should hold the lock for the whole file group in default mode' expects a lock on one test to cover the whole file.
reason: The issue proposes an option named 'locks' (a list) on the test; the tests use a singular 'lock' detail that accepts a string or array, so a fix that implements 'locks' as the issue asks fails all fail-to-pass tests. The tests also require describe-level locks, a 'details.lock' validation message, and file-group lock scope in default mode, none of which the issue states.

deciding_assertions: reporter.spec.ts '--add-reporter should append to configured reporters instead of replacing them': runs with additionalArgs ['--add-reporter=./added-reporter.js'] and expects output from both reporters.
reason: The issue asks for a CLI flag named '--append-reporter'. The test passes '--add-reporter', a name the issue never gives. A fix that adds '--append-reporter' exactly as requested fails the test (unknown option).

deciding_assertions: playwright.trace.spec.ts 'should record test annotations in trace': parseTrace(...).model.annotations toEqual [{note1, static}, {note2, dynamic}, {type: 'note3'}].
reason: The issue asks to show test annotations in the trace viewer Metadata tab. The test reads a new internal TraceModel property named 'annotations' holding a flat array of {type, description}. A reasonable fix that writes annotations into the trace and shows them in the Metadata tab, but exposes them under another model property or reads them in the UI from the context entry, fails this assertion; 'annotations' follows the testTimeout precedent, so many fixes would pass, hence medium.

deciding_assertions: browsercontext-storage-state.spec.ts 'should round-trip OPFS': storageState({opfs: true}).origins toEqual [{origin, localStorage: [], opfs: [{path: 'hello.txt', type: 'file', base64}, {path: 'nested', type: 'directory'}, {path: 'nested/data.bin', ...}, {path: 'nested/empty', type: 'directory'}]}]; global-fetch-cookie.spec.ts 'should preserve origin storage on import/export of storage state' feeds and expects the same flat {path, type, base64} entries.
reason: The issue gives the option name 'opfs' (with alternatives) and says file contents can be base64, but gives no serialization schema. The tests require one exact shape: a flat list sorted by name with '/'-joined paths, fields 'path', 'type' ('file' | 'directory') and 'base64', directories listed before their children. A reasonable fix that serializes a nested tree, or uses other field names, fails both fail-to-pass tests.

deciding_assertions: mcp/recorder.spec.ts: MCP tools 'browser_start_recording' / 'browser_stop_recording' with messages 'Recording started', 'Recording stopped. Recorded actions:' plus a ```js block, 'No actions were recorded.', 'Recording is already in progress', 'No recording in progress'; cli-devtools.spec.ts 'recording-start-stop': CLI commands 'recording-start' / 'recording-stop'; recorder-api.spec.ts 'should not amend the last action with a signal from another page': dialog signal code is ''.
reason: The issue only asks 'could we support codegen in MCP' or, as an alternative, attaching codegen to the browser extension. The tests need new tool and CLI command names, exact output and error texts, and a recorder signal fix for another page, none of which the issue gives. Any fix that picks other names, other messages, or the extension option fails the tests.

deciding_assertions: browsercontext-har.spec.ts interceptAPIRequests > should fulfill APIRequestContext requests from HAR: replayed.timing() toEqual all nine fields -1, startTime included; browsercontext-fetch.spec.ts should return timing / for https: domainLookupStart toBe 0, connectStart toBe domainLookupEnd, requestStart toBe connectEnd
reason: The issue asks for APIResponse.timing() with the shape of Request.timing() over the timings that fetch.ts already records; the narrowest fix maps those timings and passes the two fetch tests. The issue never mentions responses served from a HAR file, and the test needs all values -1 there, startTime included. A fix that leaves timing absent there, uses Request's defaults (startTime is not documented as -1), or fills a start time fails that assertion.

deciding_assertions: reporter-base.spec.ts should omit tags when omitTags is set / from failures when omitTags is set: reporter ['list', { omitTags: true }]; should omit tags via the PLAYWRIGHT_LIST_OMIT_TAGS environment variable
reason: The issue proposes an appendTags option (default true) for the list and line reporters. The tests pass a different option name, omitTags, and an environment variable PLAYWRIGHT_LIST_OMIT_TAGS that the issue never gives. The fix that the issue proposes (appendTags: false) fails all three fail-to-pass tests.

deciding_assertions: cli-core.spec.ts upload multiple files: cli('upload', front, back) as positionals; cli-parsing.spec.ts missing variadic argument: error contains "'files' argument: expected string, received undefined"; cli-help.spec.ts prints variadic command help: 'playwright-cli upload <files...>'
reason: The issue offers two shapes, a variadic positional or a repeatable --path like drop. The tests need the variadic one, so a --path fix fails the upload test. The issue also says that the variadic shape it verified reports "'files' argument: Invalid input" for a bare upload, and it does not ask to change that. The test needs the 'expected string, received undefined' message, so the variadic fix as the issue describes it fails that test.

deciding_assertions: har.spec.ts should close the context when saving the har fails: recordHar path under a regular file; context.close() rejects with /ENOTDIR|ENOENT|EEXIST/, the 'close' event fires, a second close() resolves
reason: The issue reports that context.close() hangs with recordHar on valid paths in CI. It gives no cause and never mentions a failed HAR write. The test covers only the case where the HAR save fails, and it needs close() to reject with the file system error. A fix that makes close finish by logging or ignoring the error fails rejects.toThrow, and a fix aimed at another cause of the hang does not touch this path.

deciding_assertions: screencast.spec.ts start size is ignored while tracing is active: video frames 800x600 although size 1000x750 was asked; screencast.spec.ts tracing screenshots size sets the shared capture size and tracing.spec.ts should produce screencast frames of the requested size / should respect screencast quality: context.tracing.start({ screencast: { size } }) and { screencast: { quality } }
reason: The issue expects page.screencast.start({ size }) to fill the requested frame, whether or not tracing is on, as with trace off and recordVideo. The test expects the size to be ignored, which gives an 800x600 video. The other tests pass a new tracing.start option, screencast: { size, quality }, that the issue never names (it says the trace size is not configurable). A fix that captures at the larger requested size fails the first test, and no fix from the issue alone passes the other three.

deciding_assertions: mcp/recorder.spec.ts clients sharing a context only receive their own recordings: client2 start is accepted and both transcripts kept separate; recorder-api.spec.ts and selector/locator generator specs: context._showRecorder, _startRecording, _stopRecording; messages 'Recorder is shown, close it before starting a recording.' and 'Recording is in progress, stop it before showing the recorder.'
reason: The issue offers two fixes: refuse the second start, or keep the recordings separate. The MCP test needs the separate recordings, so the refuse fix fails it. Most fail-to-pass tests call the renamed internal methods _showRecorder, _startRecording and _stopRecording in place of _enableRecorder and _disableRecorder, and two new error texts that the issue never gives, so any fix that keeps the existing names fails about 90 tests.

deciding_assertions: expect-timeout.spec.ts 'aborted mid-assertion' and 'already aborted': expect(locator).toBeVisible / expect(page).toHaveURL with { signal } must fail with the exact text 'Error: The assertion was aborted: stop it' and error.name not 'AbortError'; page-filechooser.spec.ts 'should abort with signal': waitForEvent rejection must have name 'AbortError' and cause equal to the abort reason
reason: The issue asks for a signal option on waitFor* APIs; the waiter already handled signal before the fix (the existing waitForEvent signal test passed), so the stated case works. The tests instead need signal support in expect matchers, which the issue does not name, an exact new message 'The assertion was aborted: ...', and a rejection of class AbortError with the reason in cause. A narrowest reasonable fix that adds or keeps signal on waitFor* APIs and rejects with the reason fails all three fail-to-pass tests.

deciding_assertions: test-locks.spec.ts: every fail-to-pass test declares test('...', { lock: 'shared' } or { lock: ['lock-a','lock-b'] }, ...); 'should support locks declared on a describe group' uses test.describe(..., { lock }); 'should validate lock in test details' expects output to contain 'details.lock'; 'should hold the lock for the whole file group in default mode' expects a lock on a1 to also cover a2
reason: The issue proposes a 'locks' list option, passed as an option of test(). The tests pass a 'lock' key (string or array) in test details, so a fix that implements the issue's 'locks' option fails every fail-to-pass test. The describe-level lock, the 'details.lock' error text and the rule that a lock covers the whole file group are also not in the issue.

deciding_assertions: reporter.spec.ts '--add-reporter should append to configured reporters instead of replacing them': runs with additionalArgs ['--add-reporter=./added-reporter.js'] and expects output from both reporters
reason: The issue asks for a CLI option named --append-reporter. The test passes --add-reporter, a flag that the real fix adds and the issue never gives. A fix that adds --append-reporter as asked makes the CLI reject the unknown flag and fails the test.

deciding_assertions: playwright.trace.spec.ts 'should record test annotations in trace': parseTrace(...).model.annotations toEqual [{note1, static}, {note2, dynamic}, {type: note3}]
reason: The issue asks to show static and runtime annotations in the trace viewer Metadata tab, but gives no storage location or property name. The test reads a new TraceModel property 'annotations'. A reasonable fix that records the annotations in the trace and shows them in the Metadata tab through another field or event (for example a separate trace event read by the metadata view, or a field named testAnnotations) fails this assertion. The name follows the sibling testTimeout pattern, so a reader could call it a natural choice.

deciding_assertions: browsercontext-storage-state.spec.ts 'should round-trip OPFS': storageState({ opfs: true }).origins toEqual [{ origin, localStorage: [], opfs: [{ path: 'hello.txt', type: 'file', base64 }, { path: 'nested', type: 'directory' }, { path: 'nested/data.bin', ... }, { path: 'nested/empty', type: 'directory' }] }]; global-fetch-cookie.spec.ts 'should preserve origin storage on import/export of storage state': the same flat opfs entry format round-trips through request.storageState({ indexedDB: true, opfs: true })
reason: The issue gives the option name 'opfs' and says to use base64 for file contents. It does not give the serialized format. The tests assert one exact format: a flat, sorted list with keys path (slash-joined relative path), type 'file' or 'directory', and base64. A reasonable fix that serializes OPFS as a nested tree, or with other key names or order, captures and restores OPFS correctly but fails both toEqual assertions.

deciding_assertions: mcp/recorder.spec.ts: MCP tools 'browser_start_recording' and 'browser_stop_recording' with texts 'Recording started', 'Recording stopped. Recorded actions:' plus a fenced code block, 'No actions were recorded.', 'Recording is already in progress', 'No recording in progress', and python output with --codegen=python; cli-devtools.spec.ts 'recording-start-stop': CLI commands recording-start and recording-stop; recorder-api.spec.ts 'should not amend the last action with a signal from another page': a dialog signal on page2 has empty code
reason: The issue is a vague request that offers two options: codegen in MCP, or attaching the existing codegen command to the browser extension. It gives no tool names, commands or messages. The tests need new MCP tool names, new CLI command names and exact response texts, plus a recorder signal fix that the issue does not mention. Any fix that chooses other names, the extension option, or other wording fails the fail-to-pass tests.

deciding_assertions: browsercontext-har.spec.ts interceptAPIRequests > should fulfill APIRequestContext requests from HAR: replayed.timing() toEqual an object with every field -1, including startTime: -1. (browsercontext-fetch.spec.ts should return timing / for https: domainLookupStart 0, connectStart == domainLookupEnd, requestStart == connectEnd, secureConnectionStart -1 on http.)
reason: The issue asks for APIResponse.timing() with the shape of Request.timing() for network requests and never mentions responses served from a HAR file. The narrowest reasonable fix fills timing on the network path and gives some fallback elsewhere; a fallback with startTime as the request wall time or 0 (the Request default), or no timing object, fails the HAR test, which needs startTime -1, a value the documented meaning of startTime does not give. The two fetch tests follow from mapping the already recorded socket events and pass with that fix.

deciding_assertions: reporter-base.spec.ts should omit tags when omitTags is set / from failures when omitTags is set: reporter ['list', { omitTags: true }]; should omit tags via the PLAYWRIGHT_LIST_OMIT_TAGS environment variable: env PLAYWRIGHT_LIST_OMIT_TAGS=1 hides appended tags.
reason: The issue proposes one option, appendTags (default true), used as ['list', { appendTags: false }]. The tests pass a different option name, omitTags, and a new environment variable PLAYWRIGHT_LIST_OMIT_TAGS that the issue does not give. A fix that adds appendTags exactly as the issue proposes fails all fail-to-pass tests.

deciding_assertions: cli-core.spec.ts upload multiple files: cli('upload', front, back) as positionals; cli-help.spec.ts prints variadic command help: 'playwright-cli upload <files...>'; cli-parsing.spec.ts missing variadic argument: bare upload gives "error: 'files' argument: expected string, received undefined".
reason: The issue offers two shapes (variadic positional or repeatable --path); the tests need the variadic positional and its help text, so a --path fix fails. The issue also states that its preferred variadic fix, as verified, makes bare upload report "'files' argument: Invalid input"; the test needs the old "expected string, received undefined" text, so the fix exactly as the issue proposes it fails the missing-argument test unless it also changes the union error formatting.

deciding_assertions: har.spec.ts should close the context when saving the har fails: recordHar path under a regular file; context.close() rejects with /ENOTDIR|ENOENT|EEXIST/, the 'close' event fires, and a second context.close() resolves.
reason: The issue reports a teardown hang with recordHar in CI but gives no trigger and never mentions a failed HAR write. The test checks only the save-failure path (close must reject with the fs error yet still close the context, and a repeat close must resolve); a fix aimed at another plausible hang cause in HAR recording or close does not cover it. The rejection itself follows existing code that throws the save error, so the deciding gap is the unstated trigger.

deciding_assertions: screencast.spec.ts start size is ignored while tracing is active: screencast size 1000x750 with tracing on gives a video of 800x600; tracing screenshots size sets the shared capture size: context.tracing.start({ screencast: { size } }); tracing.spec.ts should produce screencast frames of the requested size / should respect screencast quality: tracing.start({ screencast: { size } }) and ({ screencast: { quality } }).
reason: The issue expects page.screencast.start({ size }) to fill the requested frame size regardless of tracing. The test asserts the opposite: the requested size is ignored and the video is 800x600. The other tests need a new screencast option of tracing.start with size and quality, which the issue does not give (it says the trace size is not configurable). A fix that scales the capture to the requested size fails all four.

deciding_assertions: recorder-api.spec.ts and inspectorTest/locator-generator/selector-generator: calls context._showRecorder, _startRecording, _stopRecording (renamed internal API); errors 'Recorder is shown, close it before starting a recording.' and 'Recording is in progress, stop it before showing the recorder.'; mcp recorder.spec.ts clients sharing a context only receive their own recordings: client2 start succeeds and its transcript contains client1's Beta click.
reason: The issue offers two designs (refuse the second start or keep recordings separate); the MCP test needs the second and even expects client1's Beta click in client2's transcript, which the issue says should not happen. Most fail-to-pass tests fail only because they call new internal method names (_showRecorder, _startRecording, _stopRecording) and assert new error texts that the issue does not give. A fix that refuses the second start, or that keeps per-client sinks under the old names, fails these tests.
